note: Position 2 alone, then only the way across (position-neck's cross: the slide on the G string), the same crossing in C and on a string the learner picks, then improvising across both over two chords. The why says what makes the join work, so the learner can find the next one; the text names the notes of the slide and leaves the frets to the neck.

exercise.title: Join positions 1 and 2
exercise.focus: Minor pentatonic · positions 1 → 2 · a slide on the G string · A then C
exercise.why: Position 2 starts on the notes where position 1 ends, so one slide along one string carries a phrase from the first into the second.

sections.text: Press Play below to start the metronome. Play position 2 of A minor pentatonic up and back down, one note per beat, and notice where its ringed {{1}} notes sit. Keep going until the shape feels as familiar as position 1.

The neck below shows only the way from position 1 to position 2. Climb position 1 from the low {{1}}. On the G string, slide from {{4}} up to {{5}} and finish the climb in position 2. Come back down the same way, sliding from {{5}} to {{4}}.

The same crossing in C minor pentatonic, further up the neck: the slide on the G string is still {{4}} to {{5}}. The notes change, the pattern doesn't. Then tap another string beside "Cross on" under the neck and slide across there: same move, new drill.

Press Play below to start the backing, which switches between Cm7 and Fm7. Improvise across both positions, and slide from one to the other in the middle of a phrase. Land on {{c}} when Cm7 comes round and on {{f}} when Fm7 comes round.
